lines.text: So why does it snap at the water's surface?
Light from the straw speeds up as it leaves the water, and changes direction.
Like a mower rolling from grass to pavement: one side speeds up first.
Your brain traces the light back in a straight line, so the underwater part looks higher.
That's why a pool looks shallower from above: about three quarters of its real depth.
